hero.alt: Cream title card reading Can You Do Wudu With Socks On?

sources.title: Qur'an 5:6 (Surah Al-Ma'idah) on Quran.com
sources.supports: Wudu command including washing the feet to the ankles.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 182: the Prophet wiped over his khuffs during wudu on a journey
sources.supports: Al-Mughirah poured water; the Prophet washed face and forearms, wiped head, and wiped over the two khuffs.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 206: khuffs put on while the feet were pure
sources.supports: The Prophet told al-Mughirah to leave his khuffs as he had put them on after ablution while pure, then wiped over them.

sources.title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 99: wiping over socks and sandals, with jurists' views
sources.supports: Prophet wiped over jawrab and sandals; Tirmidhi hasan sahih, Darussalam da'if; Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, Shafi'i, Ahmad, Ishaq allow if thick; Abu Hanifa report.

sources.title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 96: wiping over khuffs for the traveller and resident
sources.supports: Travellers told not to remove khuffs three days and nights except for janabah; jurists hold one day and night for resident, three for traveller; some set no limit.

sources.title: Sunan an-Nasa'i 127: time limit for wiping over khuffs
sources.supports: Safwan ibn Assal: wipe over khuffs and do not remove them for three nights for defecating, urinating or sleeping, only for janabah; graded hasan.

sources.title: Sunan Abi Dawud 162: wiping the upper part of the khuff
sources.supports: Ali: if religion were by opinion the underside would be wiped, but I saw the Messenger of Allah wipe the upper part; sahih per al-Albani.

review.notes: Re-read every capture retrieved 2026-10-28 including Arabic jurist notes in Tirmidhi 96 and 99. Muslim 276 (resident duration) returned 404/403, so the resident one-day rule is attributed to the jurists listed by at-Tirmidhi rather than to a hadith. Tirmidhi 99's grading conflict (hasan sahih by at-Tirmidhi, da'if per Darussalam) is disclosed. Thin socks are presented as a scholarly difference without a universal ruling; contemporary leniency is stated generally without attribution. Abu Dawud 161 and Ibn Majah 559 were fetched but not cited. Hero generated locally with the sand palette and inspected: 1200x630 legible title card, not duplicated in body. No app CTA; links /prayer-times and existing wudu, ghusl, tayammum and passing-wind guides.

claim_checks.claim: Prophet wiped over his two khuffs during wudu on a journey
claim_checks.explanation: He 'washed his face, forearms and passed his wet hand over his head and over the two Khuff'.

claim_checks.claim: Socks must be put on while in a state of purity
claim_checks.explanation: 'He ordered me to leave them as he had put them after performing ablution. So he passed wet hands over them'; Arabic: adkhaltuhuma tahiratayn.

claim_checks.claim: Tirmidhi 99 report on socks and sandals, grading dispute, jurists allow thick socks, Abu Hanifa report
claim_checks.explanation: English text of hadith; Arabic note hasan sahih and named jurists 'idha kana thakhinayn'; Abu Muqatil's report of Abu Hanifa; Grade Da'if (Darussalam).

claim_checks.claim: Three days and nights for travellers except janabah; resident one day and night per named jurists; some set no limit
claim_checks.explanation: Safwan's narration; Arabic note: yamsahu al-muqim yawman wa laylatan wal-musafir thalathata ayyam; some scholars did not set a time. Grade Hasan.

claim_checks.claim: Same three-night limit for travellers in an-Nasa'i
claim_checks.explanation: Safwan: wipe over khuffs and not take them off for three nights for defecating, urinating or sleeping, only for janabah. Grade Hasan.

claim_checks.claim: Wipe the upper part of the khuff, per Ali
claim_checks.explanation: 'I have seen the Messenger of Allah wiping over the upper part'; Grade Sahih (Al-Albani).

claim_checks.claim: Qur'an commands washing the feet to the ankles in wudu
claim_checks.explanation: Translation: 'wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, wipe your heads, and wash your feet to the ankles.'
